newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate leader--committed to tax cut this year.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate leader--committed to tax cut this year.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Monday he was "absolutely committed" to doing a tax cut this year.

"I'm absolutely committed to doing a tax cut this year," Lott told reporters. The Mississippi Republican listed a child tax credit, and reductions in the capital gains and estate taxes as areas he would like to see action occur.

Regarding the stalled budget negotiations, Lott said a budget deal with the White House would require President Clinton's agreement to protect Medicare health care for the elderly, to back off spending increase proposals and to accept greater tax cuts.

"This isn't going to happen by immaculate conception. There is going to have to be a coming together here," Lott told reporters. He added that staff talks during the two week recess yielded no movement on key budget issues.
Lott repeated his stance that Republican leaders will work with moderate Democrats to reach a budget compromise barring agreement with the administration.
